question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

During a fire drill, (a)/ students are trained to take (b)/ shelter above the desk (c)/ within thirty seconds. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The preposition "under" is used to show a position below and covered by something, while "above" means "higher than", which is the opposite of taking cover. So "shelter above the desk" must be "shelter under the desk".

◦ Corrected sentence: During a fire drill, students are trained to take shelter under the desk within thirty seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "During a fire drill," is proper, with "during" followed by a noun phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "students are trained to take" is proper, with the passive "are trained" followed by a to-infinitive.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "within thirty seconds." is proper, with "within" showing a time limit.

 

NOTE

 

• hide under the table, sleep under a blanket (under = below and covered); a plane flying above the clouds (above = higher than, no contact).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

This report comprises of (a)/ five chapters (b)/ and a detailed (c)/ appendix at the end. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Comprise" already means "consist of" and is never followed by "of". So "comprises of" must be "comprises".

◦ Corrected sentence: This report comprises five chapters and a detailed appendix at the end.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "five chapters" is proper, with the plural noun after a number.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and a detailed" is proper, with "and" joining the two objects of "comprises".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "appendix at the end." is proper, with "at" used before "the end".

 

NOTE

 

• The book comprises ten units, The team comprises eleven players (comprise, no "of"); The report consists of five chapters (consist + of).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

They will finish loading the truck (a)/ early since they have to (b)/ set off before dawn. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Since" is used only for a point of time ("since Monday", "since 2020"), and not for a duration such as "early". Here the intended meaning is simply "because they have to set off early", so "early since" must be "early because", or "since" must be dropped and reworded.

◦ Corrected sentence: They will finish loading the truck early because they have to set off before dawn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "They will finish loading the truck" is proper, with "finish" followed by a gerund.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "set off before dawn." is proper, with "before" showing a point of time.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "since" in part (b) is wrongly used where a reason word such as "because" is needed.

 

NOTE

 

• since Monday, since 2020, since morning (since + a point of time), and not early since to mean "because".

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: It has been snowing since last night.
option_2: It has been snowing from last night.
option_3: It has been snowing by last night.
option_4: It has been snowing till last night.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. It has been snowing since last night.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An action that began at a point of time in the past and continues up to now is introduced by "since" with the present perfect (continuous). "Last night" is such a point of time, so the correct answer is "since last night".

◦ Correct sentence: It has been snowing since last night.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "from last night" — "from" marks a starting point but is not the standard preposition with the present perfect continuous for an action continuing to now.

 

• Option 3: "by last night" — "by" shows a deadline for a completed action, and it does not fit a continuing action.

 

• Option 4: "till last night" — "till" (up to a point) suggests the action has stopped, which contradicts the continuing sense of "has been snowing".

 

NOTE

 

• It has been raining since morning, She has lived here since 2015 (present perfect / present perfect continuous + since + a point of time).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The young couple got married with (a)/ each other last spring (b)/ in a small ceremony (c)/ attended only by close family. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "married to" and not "married with". So "got married with" must be "got married to".

◦ Corrected sentence: The young couple got married to each other last spring in a small ceremony attended only by close family.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "each other last spring" is proper, with "last spring" needing no preposition.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "in a small ceremony" is proper, with "in" used before an event.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "attended only by close family." is proper, with "by" showing the agent of the passive "attended".

 

NOTE

 

• He got married to his college sweetheart, She is married to a doctor (married to), and not married with.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

His handwriting (a)/ is completely (b)/ different than his elder brother's (c)/ neat, careful style. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The standard preposition after "different" is "from", and "different than" is generally avoided in formal usage. So "different than" must be "different from".

◦ Corrected sentence: His handwriting is completely different from his elder brother's neat, careful style.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "His handwriting" is proper, as the subject of the sentence.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is completely" is proper, with the adverb "completely" modifying "different".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "neat, careful style." is proper, with two adjectives joined by a comma before the noun.

 

NOTE

 

• different from (standard formal usage), and not different than, different to in formal writing.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The tourists were genuinely (a)/ interested in the local (b)/ handicrafts and folk music. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. The fixed expression is "interested in", and it is correctly used here with "the local handicrafts and folk music".

◦ Sentence as given: The tourists were genuinely interested in the local handicrafts and folk music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The tourists were genuinely" is proper, with the adverb "genuinely" modifying "interested".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "interested in the local" is proper, with "interested" correctly followed by "in".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "handicrafts and folk music." is proper, with "and" joining the two objects.

 

NOTE

 

• interested in music, interested in sports (interested + in), and not interested for, interested with.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The little boy was terrified from (a)/ the loud thunder that shook (b)/ the windows of (c)/ the old house. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "afraid / terrified of", and not "terrified from". So "terrified from" must be "terrified of".

◦ Corrected sentence: The little boy was terrified of the loud thunder that shook the windows of the old house.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the loud thunder that shook" is proper, with "that" introducing a relative clause.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the windows of" is proper, with "of" showing possession.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the old house." is proper, as the object of "of".

 

NOTE

 

• afraid of the dark, terrified of spiders, frightened of snakes (afraid / terrified / frightened + of).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The inspector accused the shopkeeper for (a)/ selling adulterated (b)/ spices to unsuspecting (c)/ customers in the market. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "accused of", and not "accused for". So "accused the shopkeeper for" must be "accused the shopkeeper of".

◦ Corrected sentence: The inspector accused the shopkeeper of selling adulterated spices to unsuspecting customers in the market.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "selling adulterated" is proper, with the gerund "selling" after "of".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "spices to unsuspecting" is proper, with "to" showing the recipient.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "customers in the market." is proper, with "in" used for a place.

 

NOTE

 

• accused of theft, accused of cheating (accused + of), and not accused for.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

My younger sister (a)/ is extremely (b)/ fond off mangoes and (c)/ eats them all summer. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "fond of", spelt with a single "o" — "off" is a different word altogether and is never used here. So "fond off" must be "fond of".

◦ Corrected sentence: My younger sister is extremely fond of mangoes and eats them all summer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "My younger sister" is proper, as the subject before the verb "is".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is extremely" is proper, with the adverb "extremely" modifying "fond".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "eats them all summer." is proper, with "them" referring to "mangoes".

 

NOTE

 

• fond of sweets, fond of music (fond + of, not "off"), and not fond off, fond with.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The nurse gently reminded the patient (a)/ of his appointment (b)/ with the cardiologist. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. The fixed expression is "remind someone of something", and it is correctly used here.

◦ Sentence as given: The nurse gently reminded the patient of his appointment with the cardiologist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The nurse gently reminded the patient" is proper, with the simple past "reminded" followed by an object.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "of his appointment" is proper, with "remind" correctly followed by "of".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "with the cardiologist." is proper, with "an appointment with" a specific person.

 

NOTE

 

• remind him of the deadline, remind her of her promise (remind + someone + of), and not remind of to, remind about for.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The new library has been built (a)/ close to the old (b)/ town hall and (c)/ stands adjacent with it. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

• Part (c) is correct — "town hall and" is proper, with "and" joining the two clauses.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The court convicted the man for (a)/ fraud after (b)/ examining the evidence (c)/ presented by the prosecution. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "convicted of" a crime, and not "convicted for". So "convicted the man for fraud" must be "convicted the man of fraud".

◦ Corrected sentence: The court convicted the man of fraud after examining the evidence presented by the prosecution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "fraud after" is proper, with "after" showing sequence.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "examining the evidence" is proper, with the gerund "examining" following "after".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "presented by the prosecution." is proper, with "by" showing the agent.

 

NOTE

 

• convicted of theft, convicted of murder (convicted + of), and not convicted for.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The train finally arrived to (a)/ the small station (b)/ two hours behind (c)/ its scheduled time. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Arrive" takes "at" before a small place or a point (a station, a village, a spot) and "in" before a large place (a city, a country). "To" is never used after "arrive". So "arrived to the small station" must be "arrived at the small station".

◦ Corrected sentence: The train finally arrived at the small station two hours behind its scheduled time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the small station" is proper, with "the" used before a specific station.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "two hours behind" is proper, with "behind" showing a delay.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "its scheduled time." is proper, with the possessive "its" agreeing with "train".

 

NOTE

 

• arrived at the airport, arrived at the venue (at + small place); arrived in Delhi, arrived in Japan (in + large place), and not arrived to.

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: The professor is very good on statistics.
option_2: The professor is very good at statistics.
option_3: The professor is very good in statistics.
option_4: The professor is very good with statistics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The professor is very good at statistics.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression for skill in a subject or activity is "good at". So the correct answer is "good at statistics".

◦ Correct sentence: The professor is very good at statistics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "good on statistics" — "on" is not the standard preposition to show skill in a subject.

 

• Option 3: "good in statistics" — "in" is commonly used before a school subject in some contexts, but the standard fixed idiom for personal skill is "good at".

 

• Option 4: "good with statistics" — "good with" is used for handling people or objects (good with children, good with tools), not for a subject of study.

 

NOTE

 

• good at maths, good at cooking, bad at spelling (good / bad + at), and not good on, good for.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The committee members (a)/ could not (b)/ agree with the new proposal for reducing (c)/ the annual membership fee. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Agree with" is used for a person, while "agree to" is used for a plan, proposal or suggestion. So "agree with the new proposal" must be "agree to the new proposal".

◦ Corrected sentence: The committee members could not agree to the new proposal for reducing the annual membership fee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The committee members" is proper, as the plural subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "could not" is proper, before the base verb "agree".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the annual membership fee." is proper, with "the" before a specific fee.

 

NOTE

 

• agree with your friend (person); agree to a plan, agree to the terms (proposal / plan); agree on a date (a shared decision).

question:

The manager insisted on (a)/ checking every invoice (b)/ before releasing the payment. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The manager insisted on" is proper, with "insisted" correctly followed by "on".

• insist on punctuality, insist on seeing the manager (insist + on), and not insist for, insist to.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The two brothers have been quarrelling for (a)/ the property (b)/ left behind by (c)/ their late father. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "quarrel about / over" a matter, and not "quarrel for". So "quarrelling for the property" must be "quarrelling over the property".

◦ Corrected sentence: The two brothers have been quarrelling over the property left behind by their late father.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the property" is proper, as the object of "over".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "left behind by" is proper, with "by" showing the person who left it.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "their late father." is proper, with "late" meaning "recently deceased" before the noun.

 

NOTE

 

• quarrel over money, quarrel about trivial matters (quarrel + over / about), and not quarrel for.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The security personnel searched (a)/ every visitor's bag (b)/ carefully for hidden (c)/ weapons for the checkpoint. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "At" is used for a specific point such as a checkpoint, gate or entrance, and not "for". So "weapons for the checkpoint" must be "weapons at the checkpoint".

◦ Corrected sentence: The security personnel searched every visitor's bag carefully for hidden weapons at the checkpoint.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The security personnel searched" is proper, with the plural "personnel" and the simple past "searched".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "every visitor's bag" is proper, with the possessive "'s" before "bag".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "carefully for hidden" is proper, with "search for" correctly used to mean "look for".

 

NOTE

 

• at the checkpoint, at the gate, at the entrance (at + a specific point), and not for the checkpoint.

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: Visitors are prohibited to smoke inside the building.
option_2: Visitors are prohibited for smoking inside the building.
option_3: Visitors are prohibited from smoking inside the building.
option_4: Visitors are prohibited on smoking inside the building.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Visitors are prohibited from smoking inside the building.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "prohibited from + gerund", and not "to / for / on". So the correct answer is "prohibited from smoking".

◦ Correct sentence: Visitors are prohibited from smoking inside the building.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "prohibited to smoke" — "to" is not the preposition used with "prohibited"; only "from" is standard.

 

• Option 2: "prohibited for smoking" — "for" is not the preposition used with "prohibited".

 

• Option 4: "prohibited on smoking" — "on" is not used with "prohibited".

 

NOTE

 

• prohibited from entering, prohibited from parking here (prohibited + from + gerund), and not prohibited to, prohibited for.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The old bridge collapsed after colliding against (a)/ a heavily (b)/ loaded cargo (c)/ vessel. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "collide with", and not "collide against". So "colliding against" must be "colliding with".

◦ Corrected sentence: The old bridge collapsed after colliding with a heavily loaded cargo vessel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "a heavily" is proper, with the adverb "heavily" modifying "loaded".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "loaded cargo" is proper, with "cargo" used as an adjective before "vessel".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "vessel." is proper, as the object of "with".

 

NOTE

 

• collide with a truck, collide with another vehicle (collide + with), and not collide against.

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The young entrepreneur" is proper, as a singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "a profitable business" is proper, with "a" before the consonant sound of "profitable".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "within just two years." is proper, with "within" showing a time limit.

 

NOTE

 

• succeed in passing the exam, succeed in convincing them (succeed + in + gerund), and not succeed to.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Villagers in this region depend (a)/ mostly on (b)/ agriculture of (c)/ their daily livelihood. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression to show purpose here is "depend on … for", and not "of". So "agriculture of their daily livelihood" must be "agriculture for their daily livelihood".

◦ Corrected sentence: Villagers in this region depend mostly on agriculture for their daily livelihood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Villagers in this region depend" is proper, with the plural verb "depend" agreeing with "villagers".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "mostly on" is proper, with "depend on" as the fixed expression.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "their daily livelihood." is proper, with the plural possessive "their" agreeing with "villagers".

 

NOTE

 

• depend on agriculture for their livelihood, rely on savings for emergencies (depend / rely on … for), and not depend on … of.
